2 & 3 Nov

Riemann sum and definite integrals

The schedule also lists a review of Calculus midterm 1 for these two classes. That paper, with worked answers, is under Past midterms on the Calculus midterm 1 page.

  • The idea: to find the area under y=f(x)y=f(x)y=f(x) from x=ax=ax=a to x=bx=bx=b, cut it into nnn thin strips, treat each strip as a rectangle, add up the rectangles, and let n→∞n\to\inftyn→∞.
  • Strip width and sample points: every strip has the same width Δx=b−an\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}Δx=nb−a​ Strip kkk (for k=1,2,…,nk=1,2,\dots,nk=1,2,…,n) runs from a+(k−1)Δxa+(k-1)\Delta xa+(k−1)Δx to a+kΔxa+k\Delta xa+kΔx. Its height is f(xk)f(x_k)f(xk​) at one point xkx_kxk​ of the strip: right end: xk=a+k Δxleft end: xk=a+(k−1) Δxmidpoint: xk=a+(k−12)Δx\begin{aligned}\text{right end: }x_k&=a+k\,\Delta x\\[2pt]\text{left end: }x_k&=a+(k-1)\,\Delta x\\[2pt]\text{midpoint: }x_k&=a+\left(k-\tfrac{1}{2}\right)\Delta x\end{aligned}right end: xk​left end: xk​midpoint: xk​​=a+kΔx=a+(k−1)Δx=a+(k−21​)Δx​ So xkx_kxk​ says where strip kkk is, and f(xk)f(x_k)f(xk​) how tall it is. The slides write NNN for the number of strips: it is the same as nnn here.
  • Riemann sum and definite integral: Sn=∑k=1nf(xk) Δx∫abf(x) dx=lim⁡n→∞Sn\begin{gathered}S_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}f(x_k)\,\Delta x\\[6pt]\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\lim_{n\to\infty}S_n\end{gathered}Sn​=k=1∑n​f(xk​)Δx∫ab​f(x)dx=n→∞lim​Sn​​ The sign ∫\int∫ is a stretched S for "sum", and dxdxdx comes from Δx\Delta xΔx. Here aaa is the lower limit and bbb the upper limit. Left ends, right ends and midpoints all give the same limit. The result is a number, so the letter for the variable doesn't matter: ∫02x2 dx=∫02t2 dt.\int_0^2x^2\,dx=\int_0^2t^2\,dt.∫02​x2dx=∫02​t2dt.
  • Partial sums: the sum for x2x^2x2 needs the partial sum of k2k^2k2, and the one for x3x^3x3 that of k3k^3k3: ∑k=1n1=n∑k=1nk=n(n+1)2∑k=1nk2=n(n+1)(2n+1)6∑k=1nk3=n2(n+1)24\begin{aligned}\sum_{k=1}^{n}1&=n\\[2pt]\sum_{k=1}^{n}k&=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\\[2pt]\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^2&=\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}\\[2pt]\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^3&=\frac{n^2(n+1)^2}{4}\end{aligned}k=1∑n​1k=1∑n​kk=1∑n​k2k=1∑n​k3​=n=2n(n+1)​=6n(n+1)(2n+1)​=4n2(n+1)2​​ A constant comes out of the sum: ∑c ak=c∑ak.\sum c\,a_k=c\sum a_k.∑cak​=c∑ak​. With left ends, ∑k=1n(k−1)2=02+12+⋯+(n−1)2,\sum_{k=1}^{n}(k-1)^2=0^2+1^2+\dots+(n-1)^2,∑k=1n​(k−1)2=02+12+⋯+(n−1)2, so replace nnn by n−1n-1n−1 in the formula.
  • Five steps: find Δx\Delta xΔx, write xkx_kxk​, work out f(xk)f(x_k)f(xk​), add up with the partial sums (constants out first), then let n→∞n\to\inftyn→∞. When a≠0a\ne0a=0, expand f(a+kΔx)f(a+k\Delta x)f(a+kΔx) and split it into separate sums.
  • Upper and lower sums: when fff is increasing, right ends give the upper sum and left ends the lower sum: lower sum<area<upper sum\text{lower sum}<\text{area}<\text{upper sum}lower sum<area<upper sum Both tend to the same number as n→∞n\to\inftyn→∞, and that number is the area. For a decreasing fff it is the other way round.
  • The class example, x2x^2x2 from 000 to LLL (right ends, xk=kLnx_k=\frac{kL}{n}xk​=nkL​): Sn=L3n3∑k=1nk2=L36⋅(n+1)(2n+1)n2→L36⋅2=L33\begin{aligned}S_n&=\frac{L^3}{n^3}\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^2\\[4pt]&=\frac{L^3}{6}\cdot\frac{(n+1)(2n+1)}{n^2}\\[4pt]&\to\frac{L^3}{6}\cdot2=\frac{L^3}{3}\end{aligned}Sn​​=n3L3​k=1∑n​k2=6L3​⋅n2(n+1)(2n+1)​→6L3​⋅2=3L3​​ That is one third of the L×L2L\times L^2L×L2 box around the region. The exercise, x3x^3x3 from 000 to LLL, gives Sn=L44(1+1n)2→L44.S_n=\frac{L^4}{4}\left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right)^2\to\frac{L^4}{4}.Sn​=4L4​(1+n1​)2→4L4​. The pattern: ∫0Lxm dx=Lm+1m+1\int_0^L x^m\,dx=\frac{L^{m+1}}{m+1}∫0L​xmdx=m+1Lm+1​
  • Quick way: for xmx^mxm on [0,L][0,L][0,L] the first four steps collapse into one line: Sn=(Ln)m+1∑k=1nkmS_n=\left(\frac{L}{n}\right)^{m+1}\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^mSn​=(nL​)m+1k=1∑n​km As n→∞n\to\inftyn→∞ only the highest power of nnn counts: ∑k≈n22,\sum k\approx\frac{n^2}{2},∑k≈2n2​, ∑k2≈n33,\sum k^2\approx\frac{n^3}{3},∑k2≈3n3​, ∑k3≈n44,\sum k^3\approx\frac{n^4}{4},∑k3≈4n4​, and (n+1)(2n+1)n2→2.\frac{(n+1)(2n+1)}{n^2}\to2.n2(n+1)(2n+1)​→2. Write SnS_nSn​ out in full first: the limit is the last step.
  • Signed area: where f<0f<0f<0, the terms f(xk)Δxf(x_k)\Delta xf(xk​)Δx are negative, so the integral is the area above the xxx-axis minus the area below it. For the actual area, split at the zeros of fff and add the parts as positive numbers.
  • The class example, x2+x−2x^2+x-2x2+x−2 on [0,2][0,2][0,2]: f=(x+2)(x−1)f=(x+2)(x-1)f=(x+2)(x−1) is negative on [0,1)[0,1)[0,1) and positive on (1,2](1,2](1,2]. With right ends, Sn=23+6n+43n2→23S_n=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{6}{n}+\frac{4}{3n^2}\to\frac{2}{3}Sn​=32​+n6​+3n24​→32​ The integral 23\frac{2}{3}32​ is 116\frac{11}{6}611​ above the axis (from 111 to 222) minus 76\frac{7}{6}67​ below it (from 000 to 111), but the area of the region is 116+76=3.\frac{11}{6}+\frac{7}{6}=3.611​+67​=3. Practice works it out step by step.
  • Any interval [a,b][a,b][a,b]: joining two intervals adds their integrals, so ∫abf(x) dx=∫0bf(x) dx−∫0af(x) dx\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\int_0^b f(x)\,dx-\int_0^a f(x)\,dx∫ab​f(x)dx=∫0b​f(x)dx−∫0a​f(x)dx With the results on [0,L][0,L][0,L]: ∫abxm dx=bm+1−am+1m+1\int_a^b x^m\,dx=\frac{b^{m+1}-a^{m+1}}{m+1}∫ab​xmdx=m+1bm+1−am+1​ For example ∫12x2 dx=8−13=73.\int_1^2x^2\,dx=\frac{8-1}{3}=\frac{7}{3}.∫12​x2dx=38−1​=37​.
  • Properties: for any order of aaa, bbb and ccc, ∫aaf dx=0∫baf dx=−∫abf dx∫abf dx+∫bcf dx=∫acf dx∫abc dx=c (b−a)\begin{aligned}\int_a^a f\,dx&=0\\[2pt]\int_b^a f\,dx&=-\int_a^b f\,dx\\[2pt]\int_a^b f\,dx+\int_b^c f\,dx&=\int_a^c f\,dx\\[2pt]\int_a^b c\,dx&=c\,(b-a)\end{aligned}∫aa​fdx∫ba​fdx∫ab​fdx+∫bc​fdx∫ab​cdx​=0=−∫ab​fdx=∫ac​fdx=c(b−a)​ Sums split and constants come out: ∫ab(αf+βg) dx=α∫abf dx+β∫abg dx\int_a^b(\alpha f+\beta g)\,dx=\alpha\int_a^b f\,dx+\beta\int_a^b g\,dx∫ab​(αf+βg)dx=α∫ab​fdx+β∫ab​gdx And with a≤ba\le ba≤b: if f≤gf\le gf≤g on [a,b][a,b][a,b], then ∫abf dx≤∫abg dx.\int_a^b f\,dx\le\int_a^b g\,dx.∫ab​fdx≤∫ab​gdx.
  • Definite integral and antiderivative: ∫abf(x) dx\int_a^b f(x)\,dx∫ab​f(x)dx is a number, defined by Riemann sums. An antiderivative FFF, with F′=fF'=fF′=f, is a function. They meet in ∫abf(x) dx=F(b)−F(a)\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=F(b)-F(a)∫ab​f(x)dx=F(b)−F(a) because the area A(L)A(L)A(L) from 000 to LLL has A′(L)=f(L)A'(L)=f(L)A′(L)=f(L): for f(x)=x2f(x)=x^2f(x)=x2, A(L)=L33A(L)=\frac{L^3}{3}A(L)=3L3​ and A′(L)=L2A'(L)=L^2A′(L)=L2. Primitive functions are the next lesson.
  • No formula for FFF: every elementary function can be differentiated by the rules, but some have no antiderivative made of elementary functions, such as sin⁡xx\frac{\sin x}{x}xsinx​ and e−x2e^{-x^2}e−x2. Their integrals still exist, because a continuous function is integrable. For example ∫01sin⁡xx dx≈0.946\int_0^1\frac{\sin x}{x}\,dx\approx0.946∫01​xsinx​dx≈0.946 (with the value 111 at x=0x=0x=0), from a Riemann sum or from its Taylor series integrated term by term. That is why the Riemann sum is the definition, and F(b)−F(a)F(b)-F(a)F(b)−F(a) the shortcut when FFF is known.

Watch out

  • Δx=b−an.\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}.Δx=nb−a​. It is 1n\frac{1}{n}n1​ only when the interval has length 111.
  • When a≠0a\ne0a=0, keep the aaa in xk=a+kΔxx_k=a+k\Delta xxk​=a+kΔx, and expand before you split the sum.
  • A constant is added nnn times: ∑k=1n3=3n,\sum_{k=1}^{n}3=3n,∑k=1n​3=3n, not 333. In the class example the −2-2−2 gives −4-4−4 in SnS_nSn​, not −4n-\frac{4}{n}−n4​.
  • Left ends use k−1k-1k−1: ∑k=1n(k−1)=(n−1)n2.\sum_{k=1}^{n}(k-1)=\frac{(n-1)n}{2}.∑k=1n​(k−1)=2(n−1)n​.
  • "Compute the Riemann sum" asks for SnS_nSn​ as a formula in nnn. Write it out before you take the limit, and don't replace it with F(b)−F(a)F(b)-F(a)F(b)−F(a).
  • An integral is a signed area: ∫02(x−1) dx=0,\mathord{\int_0^2(x-1)\,dx}=0,∫02​(x−1)dx=0, yet the region between the line and the axis has area 111.
  • On [a,b][a,b][a,b], subtract the part from 000 to aaa: ∫12x2 dx=83−13,\int_1^2x^2\,dx=\frac{8}{3}-\frac{1}{3},∫12​x2dx=38​−31​, not 83\frac{8}{3}38​.
  • Swapping the limits changes the sign: ∫20x dx=−2\int_2^0x\,dx=-2∫20​xdx=−2.

Exam-day habits

  • Write Δx\Delta xΔx and xkx_kxk​ first, then f(xk)f(x_k)f(xk​). Most mistakes happen in these two lines.
  • Take constants out of every sum before you use a partial-sum formula, and remember ∑k=1nc=cn.\sum_{k=1}^{n}c=cn.∑k=1n​c=cn.
  • Give SnS_nSn​ as a formula in nnn, then take the limit. If you know an antiderivative, check the value with F(b)−F(a)F(b)-F(a)F(b)−F(a).
  • When fff changes sign, find its zeros first: the integral and the area of the region are different answers.
  • Keep answers exact: 163\frac{16}{3}316​, not 5.335.335.33.
